extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (educational institutions) and Title IX personnel (Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for designing and operating Title IX grievance processes, including role separation, training, evidentiary standards, appeals, informal resolution, timing, and related procedural protections for K–12 and postsecondary recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of the single investigator model / separation of investigative and adjudicative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(7)(i) prohibits the same person from serving as both the investigator (or Title IX Coordinator) and the decision-maker; investigative and adjudicative functions must be performed by different individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: separating functions reduces risk/perception of bias, increases reliability of fact-finding, and promotes sound bases for responsibility determinations. The Department rejected hybrid approaches (e.g., allowing two investigators to serve as decision-makers) as insufficient. The rule still permits the Title IX Coordinator to serve as the investigator, but the decision-maker must be a different person. Decision-makers should assess evidence and credibility impartially and must not have participated as investigator or Title IX Coordinator in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust training and impartiality requirements for Title IX personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires robust training and impartiality requirements for all individuals serving as Title IX Coordinators, investigators, or decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training materials used to train Title IX personnel must not rely on sex stereotypes. The Department believes these measures will promote consistent outcomes and reduce risks from untrained or biased personnel. Training is intended to ensure impartiality and reliability of fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator's investigative report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(5)(vii) requires the investigator to prepare an investigative report that fairly summarizes all relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigative report ensures the parties and the decision-maker are aware of the evidence gathered during the investigation and supports transparency and reliability in adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to assert bias/conflict and availability of appeals to a different decision-maker
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(8) requires recipients to offer appeals for both parties and explicitly permits either party to assert that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals serve as an additional check on alleged bias; the appeal must be to a decision-maker who did not serve in the prior role (investigator, Title IX Coordinator, or initial decision-maker). The Department revised §106.45(b)(8) to require appeals equally to both parties and to require reasonably prompt time frames for appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified appeal bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be offered equally to both parties on three specified bases: procedural irregularity, newly discovered evidence, or conflict of interest or bias on the part of Title IX personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide an appeal process addressing these narrow grounds; appeal decision-makers cannot be the same person who reached the original determination, the Title IX Coordinator, or the investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution must be voluntary and cannot be conditioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(9) forbids recipients from requiring parties to participate in informal resolution and precludes conditioning enrollment, employment, or rights on a party's participation in informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolutions may resolve allegations without full investigation/adjudication, and may involve fewer facilitators, but must be voluntarily agreed to by each party. Recipients cannot coerce participation or use informal resolution to avoid the formal grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings required (postsecondary) and role separation supports cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(6)(i) provides for live hearings in the postsecondary context; the Department considers live hearings a critical part of a fair process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating investigative and adjudicative roles is important for effective live cross-examination because a decision-maker who also investigated may be biased toward their own investigative recommendations. Live hearings allow parties to probe credibility and are part of ensuring fairness in postsecondary adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frame for completing the grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(1)(v) requires that the grievance process be completed within a reasonably prompt time frame, including completion of a live hearing (for postsecondary institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While separation of roles may lengthen the process in some cases, recipients must still complete grievance proceedings reasonably promptly. The Department revised related provisions to ensure appeals also have reasonably prompt time frames.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient choice of standard of evidence (two allowed) and consistent application
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(1)(vii) authorizes recipients to select either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard to reach determinations regarding responsibility; the selected standard must be applied consistently to all formal complaints alleging Title IX sexual harassment and regardless of whether the respondent is a student or an employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to permit 'beyond a reasonable doubt.' Recipients may choose between the two civil standards; the grievance process (including standard of evidence) should not vary based on the identity or status of the respondent. The final regulations removed NPRM language that would have limited choice of standard based on standards used for non-sexual misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator responsibilities and permitted roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8(a) requires recipients to designate a Title IX Coordinator who coordinates efforts to comply with the final regulations, responds to reports and complaints, informs complainants of supportive measures and formal complaint process, and coordinates implementation of supportive measures and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator may serve as the investigator but may not be the decision-maker on a formal complaint in which they participated; signing a formal complaint by a Title IX Coordinator does not automatically render them biased, but they must comply with impartiality and other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for treatment records
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.45(b)(5)(i) prohibits the recipient from accessing, considering, disclosing, or otherwise using a party's treatment records without the party's voluntary, written consent, even if the records are relevant to the allegations in a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This privacy protection limits evidence sources and requires voluntary consent for use of treatment records; it reflects a balance between relevance and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient autonomy balanced with uniform procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients retain flexibility (e.g., whether to use a panel or single decision-maker, whether to use employees or outsource), but that autonomy is balanced against Title IX goals of reliable fact-finding, fairness, and accuracy; the Department rejected categorical exemptions based on recipient size, complaint volume, or sanction severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may tailor policies to community needs, but cannot contravene the prohibition on a single investigator/decision-maker or other required protections; recipients' agreements (CBAs, handbooks) must conform to federal Title IX obligations as a condition of receiving federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to employees and interaction with Title VII and employment practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition of the single investigator model and the grievance process requirements apply to all recipients and to both student and employee respondents; the final regulations apply to any person in an education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use site administrators as investigators or decision-makers, but the site administrator cannot serve as both investigator and decision-maker in the same case. While Title VII and state laws may also apply, Title IX obligations are not obviated by state law; recipients often must comply with both frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to assert bias during investigation and appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: Either party may assert that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias, and §106.45(b)(8) permits parties to raise such claims and seek review by a different decision-maker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural protection that reinforces impartiality; combined with training and role separation, it is meant to increase fairness of proceedings. Parties retain the right to assert bias both before/during investigation and on appeal.
